title: Gulab Jamun: Milk Dumplings in Cardamom and Saffron Syrup
summary: Soft milk-powder dumplings fried low and slow until deep brown, then soaked in a warm cardamom, saffron and lemon syrup.

ingredients.item: ghee, plus extra for your hands
whole milk, plus a little extra if needed
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)

steps.title: Make the syrup
steps.text: Warm the sugar, water, cardamom pods and saffron in the medium pan, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Boil for 5 min until lightly syrupy but not thick. Off the heat stir in the lemon juice and rose water if using, then cover to keep warm.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Mix the milk powder, flour, baking powder and ground cardamom in the bowl. Rub in the ghee until it looks like damp sand, then add the yoghurt and most of the milk and bring together gently with your fingertips into a soft, slightly sticky dough. Add the remaining milk a teaspoon at a time only if dry. Do not knead. Cover and rest for 10 min.

steps.title: Shape the balls
steps.text: Grease your palms with ghee and roll the dough into 16 balls of about 25 g each. Roll each one until completely smooth: cracks open up in the oil. Keep them covered.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Heat the oil in the heavy pan to 145 °C. Keep it between 140 and 150 °C throughout, adjusting the heat as you go.

steps.title: Fry slowly
steps.text: Fry one test ball first, then 5 or 6 at a time, for 8-10 min, stirring the oil gently so they roll and colour evenly to a deep brown. They will swell a little. Cut the test ball open: the centre should be soft and cake-like right through. If it browns in under 6 min the oil is too hot and the middles will stay doughy.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Drain each batch on the kitchen paper for 1 min, then drop into the warm syrup. Cover and leave for at least 2 h, turning occasionally, so they absorb the syrup and swell.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve at room temperature or warmed gently in the syrup, with a little syrup spooned over and pistachio slivers on top.

tips: A soft, barely sticky dough gives soft jamun; a dry dough gives hard ones.
Never add hot jamun to boiling syrup, or they can split.
Use a thermometer; temperature control is the key to a cooked centre.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep in their syrup, covered, in the fridge for up to 5 days. Warm gently before serving.
